title: Golden Sour Cream Corn Muffins
summary: Lightly sweet corn muffins made tender with soured cream, baked to deep golden domes.
equipment: paper muffin cases or butter for greasing

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Put a shelf in the middle of the oven and heat it to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Line or grease the 12-hole tin while it warms up.

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.text: Whisk the flour, cornmeal, baking powder, bicarbonate and salt in a large bowl. Two leaveners work together here: the bicarbonate reacts with the acidic soured cream, and the baking powder adds a second lift in the oven.

steps.title: Build the wet mix
steps.text: Beat the eggs in the second bowl, then add the sugar and whisk for about 1 min until pale and thick. Pour in the melted butter slowly while whisking, followed by the soured cream and milk. Adding the butter gradually keeps the mixture smooth instead of greasy.

steps.title: Fold gently
steps.text: Pour the wet mix over the dry and fold with a spatula until just a few streaks of flour remain. A slightly lumpy batter is exactly what you want, because extra mixing makes the crumb dense.

steps.title: Fill the tin
steps.text: Share the batter between the 12 holes so each is about three-quarters full.

steps.title: Bake to golden
steps.text: Bake for 16-20 min, rotating the tin halfway through. Look for deep golden domes that spring back when pressed and a cocktail stick in the centre that comes out clean, at about 96 °C inside.

steps.title: Cool and serve
steps.text: Let the muffins rest in the tin for 5 min, then transfer them to the rack. They are lovely warm with butter or at room temperature.

tips: Fine cornmeal gives a tender crumb; coarse polenta makes the muffins gritty.
A common mistake is overbaking: start checking at 16 min, because cornmeal muffins dry out quickly once fully set.
If you have no soured cream, thick plain yoghurt works in the same quantity.
Weigh the flour and cornmeal for the most reliable texture.
storage: Store airtight at room temperature for up to 2 days or freeze for up to 1 month. Warm thawed muffins in a 150 °C oven for 5-8 min. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
